All the buffalo in Serengeti vs all the lions in Serengeti

Neither. It would be a standoff.

There are about 4000 lions in the Serengeti. There are about 16000 Cape Buffalo in the Serengeti.

About 1/3 of each population isn't mature, so we can count that as largely equal. However, usually the female lions do the hunting.

Unfortunately, buffalo don't usually kill lions. The 16000 can easily defend themselves vs. so few lions. Putting them all in one area means the larger buffalo will drink all the water and eat all the vegetation. The lions will get thirsty and move on, probably before the buffalo do - depending on the water supply and food supply.

Lions simply can't sustain a prolonged attack against a massive herd of buffalo. Buffalo don't normally kill lions. This means nobody wins.

Now, if you cram them all into a room and somehow inspire them to fight, the buffalo are going to do some serious lion stomping. It regularly takes about a half hour for a lion to kill a downed mature buffalo. Buffalo are pretty big and rather tough.
